items: Fall salmon fishing is fair on Nehalem, Tillamook, and Nestucca bays although fishing did slow a little over the past week. All basins are still producing Chinook and coho salmon. The North Coast rivers are still at low flows, so fishing is best in the bays and tidewaters. Wednesday 10/28/2026 will be the last day of wild coho retention on these basins, no wild coho adults may be retained after that date. See the regulation updates online at Fall Coastal Salmon Management for details on seasons and bag limits.

The Nestucca and Wilson Rivers still have summer steelhead available, mostly in the upper reaches. Fall can be a good time to target these fish that have been holding most of the summer, as the dropping water temperatures and fall rains can get them more active and willing to bite.
Many coastal streams are open for cutthroat trout fishing through Oct 31. There are resident and sea-run cutthroat available for catching. Check the regulations for open areas.
Trout stocking has been completed in North Coast lakes for the year, but there are still hold-over trout available to catch in many of the lakes.

Fall Chinook fishing is fair in the Siletz, Alsea, Siuslaw, Yaquina and Salmon rivers. Coho are being caught in the Siletz and Yaquina rivers. Wild coho retention in the Yaquina basin closes Oct 25. The Siuslaw closed for wild coho retention Oct 13. Refer to Fall Coastal Salmon Management for more information on season outlines and bag limits.
Siltcoos and Tahkenitch lakes are open for wild coho retention. Some early fish may be around, but the majority won't show up until we receive some measurable rain.

Weather has been near perfect for some late season trout fishing on either Garrison or Floras Lakes. Garrison Lake in particular usually has some fairly good numbers of trout that carry over from the spring stockings.
Anglers are still picking up fall chinook trolling the Chetco River estuary.
Empire, Saunders, and Butterfield Lakes will be stocked by end of week 10/23/26 with legal trout.

Coho salmon are moving into the lower parts of the North Santiam. Spinners such as Blue Fox are usually effective but bobbers and eggs will work as well. Best sections currently are from Green's Bridge down to Jefferson, as well as further down into the mainstem of the Santiam River.

Walleye fishing has been good along stretches of the Willamette River from Peoria downstream to Independence. A jet boat is the best option for getting at fish on some stretches, but fishing in 12-18 feet of water, especially trolling a worm spinner downstream a little faster than the currant has been netting some good-sized walleye.
Following trophy trout stockings, the Fall River has been fishing exceptionally well.
Pine Nursery Pond in Bend was recently stocked with brown trout.

Tiger Muskie fishing at Phillips Reservoir should be good as fish are aggressively feeding to stock up on forage before winter sets in. Water temperature is prime right now in the low 50°F. Fishing should remain hot until water temps drop below 45°F. As an added bonus, the low water levels will concentrate fish and may make catching fish easier.
Coho fishing has been great on the lower Umatilla River. Expect fishing to remain good into November. Summer steelhead are also present and will become more prominent as the season progresses.

Anglers are catching steelhead in both the Grande Ronde and Imnaha Rivers. Focus lower on both rivers this time of year. Kokanee anglers are finding bright fish on the north end of Wallowa Lake. These kokanee will be smaller in size as many larger fish are spawning at the other end of the lake. Kinney Lake was stocked for the winter with trout.
Fishing for trout at Lost Creek Reservoir.

Malheur Reservoir – great for Rainbow Trout from 10-22". Common sizes are 12-16" but fish up to 22" were captured in our sampling this week. We also fly-fished it in the evening and morning and had catches of 10+ trout/hr. People were observed being successful trolling and bank fishing with bait too. Water temperatures were in the mid 50's. You can launch a boat from the boat ramp. Water is up to the old school bus (a school bus frame in the reservoir used by those who are familiar with it to gauge how full the reservoir is).

Yellowjacket Reservoir – Great fishing without a crowd! We sampled this last week and found fish from 8-18" with a common size of 12-15". We fished leech patterns under an indicator mid-day and had non-stop action. Water temperatures are in the mid-50's here too.
Yellow perch angling continues to be excellent in numerous locations in the Klamath Basin including Crystal Creek, Fourmile Canal, Sevenmile Canal and Williamson River.
Fishing for Redband-Rainbow Trout in the Klamath River is good for fly and lure fisherman.

Many waterbodies will close after October 31 in the Klamath Basin to protect spawning Redband Trout and Chinook Salmon. This is your last chance to catch and release some monster Redband Trout that have been coming from Upper Klamath Lake this year.
Crappie angling has been excellent at Dog Lake recently.
Current and upcoming fishing opportunities:
Angling for coho has been fair to good near the mouths of some tributaries.
Forecasts for 2026 Columbia River Spring Chinook, Summer Chinook, Fall Chinook, Coho, and Sockeye are available here.

The Oregon Health Authority has issued consumption guidelines for parts of the Columbia River due to high levels of mercury and/or PCBs. Fish with these chemicals look, act, smell and taste like any other fish, so caution is important.

Salmon, steelhead, and shad. On Saturday's (10/17) effort count, there were 97 boats from Lemon Island to Fisher Island.

Marine fishing. Port by port reports for the week beginning Oct 12 :
Marine fishing. Last week, most of the coast experienced typical fall transition conditions, with large swell limiting the number of good days to get out on the water.
Marine fishing. Garibaldi: Anglers landed 2.5 rockfish on average, mostly black rockfish and yellowtail rockfishes. Lingcod landings were just below 1 fish per angler.
Marine fishing. Depoe Bay: Landings averaged 3.1 rockfish per angler, with mostly black, canary, deacon and yellowtail rockfishes landed. Lingcod catches were 1.25 fish per angler.
Marine fishing. Newport: Anglers landed 3 rockfish per person, mostly black, deacon, and canary rockfishes were observed. Lingcod was slow.
Marine fishing. Charleston: Anglers landed 3.5 rockfish, consisting of mainly black, canary, widow, and yellowtail rockfishes. Lingcod landings were 1.2 fish per angler.
Marine fishing. Brookings: Anglers caught 2.6 rockfish on average; mainly black rockfish were landed. Lingcod was slow at 0.33 fish per angler.

Marine fishing. Reminder: Ocean salmon anglers are reminded that they are limited to one rod, and no more than two single point, single shank, barbless hooks (no treble hooks) and that retention of jack salmon is not allowed in the ocean.
Marine fishing. Leadbetter Point, WA to Cape Falcon, OR

Marine fishing. Ocean salmon fishing is closed in the recreational fishery in the area from Leadbetter Point, Washington to Cape Falcon, Oregon. Possession of salmon on board a vessel is prohibited in the Columbia River Subarea.
Marine fishing. Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain
Marine fishing. Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain remains open through October 31, 2026, for all salmon except coho, with a daily bag limit of 2 salmon. The minimum size limit for Chinook is 24".
Marine fishing. Humbug Mountain to the OR/CA border
Marine fishing. The area from Humbug Mountain to the Oregon/California border is closed to ocean salmon fishing for the remainder of the year.

Marine fishing. Lingcod and many other bottomfish species are available year-round to shore anglers fishing in rocky areas. A common setup for lingcod is a jig head with a rubber swim bait – it's simple but effective. Also pack a measuring device for lingcod: the minimum legal size is 22 inches.

Marine fishing. Surfperch are available in the surf year-round along sandy beaches and rocky shores, with the best fishing (and safest fishing) occurring when swells are small. Find surfperch and other learn to fish workshops and events here .

Marine fishing. When fishing from shore or inside estuaries and bays, it is important to check the tide. Many fish that swim into estuaries and bays, including salmon, surfperch, and Pacific herring, tend to come in with the tide. Catch of these species is more likely to occur closer to slack tide. Additionally, the accessibility of some areas can be completely dependent on the tide. Do not allow the incoming tide to become a safety issue.
